page: Microsoft Azure L2aos_v4 is a storage-capable virtual machine belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and is bundled with 1440 GB of local storage. It is also Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is strong, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is weak, landing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is mixed; write speeds for large blocks are average, but read-only small block bandwidth is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also show weak to poor performance, with PassMark database operations scoring in the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of the L2aos_v4 is its high local storage capacity relative to its limited compute and memory resources. While the 1440 GB of local storage provides significant space, the 2 vCPU limit restricts its utility for highly parallelized workloads, software compilation, or intensive database operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a dense storage profile for workloads requiring large local disk space without demanding high multi-threaded compute power. It is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight file serving, basic text processing, or workloads that require substantial local storage capacity but have low CPU utilization.
